reportSubtitle: First bi-weekly look with Google and Meta running together
summary:
First report covering both Google and Meta side by side. Spent $576 across the two channels and got 3 booking inquiries. Google did the heavy lifting on cost efficiency at $107 per inquiry. Meta hit more eyeballs (13.6K impressions vs 520 on Google) but converted at a lower rate while we're still working on the creative side.

Bigger structural changes this period: switched Google off Smart Bidding to manual CPC, set bids per keyword based on top-of-page estimates, and added UTM tagging so PostHog can finally attribute Google traffic. Next report will show the full Google funnel from impression through booking for the first time.

metrics.label: Google CPA
metrics.note: 2 inquiries on $214. Held steady from prior 14-day window.

metrics.label: Meta CPA
metrics.note: 1 inquiry on $362. Creative is the bottleneck (see findings).

funnel.title: Funnel by channel
funnel.notes: Google funnel only shows 3 steps because UTM attribution to PostHog wasn't in place this period. Fixed on Jun 1; next report will show the full impression-to-booking path.

data.note: Google only — Meta launched in this period and is shown separately below. CPA held at ~$107 for the second period running. CTR dipped this period along with click volume, which lines up with the algorithm pulling back as it ran out of conversion signal.

91% of spend went to one broad-match keyword. This is what drove the move to manual CPC — the algorithm was concentrating because it didn't have enough conversion volume to optimize across the rest. Next report will show how the distribution shifts under manual bids.

findings.title: Funnel landing page is converting better than the main site
findings.description: The ad pointed at book.mobilecraftbars.com converted at 7.14% with a $100 CPA. The ad pointed at www.mobilecraftbars.com converted at 5.26% with a $113 CPA. Small sample, but directionally the discovery call funnel is doing what it was built to do.

findings.title: Meta video creative is the bottleneck on that channel
findings.description: Both Meta ads under 1% link CTR (industry norm is 1-1.5%). 83% of viewers stop watching after the first 3 seconds. Meta is also flagging Nice_Waiters as below-average creative quality, which inflates CPMs further. Audience size isn't the issue — the hooks aren't earning the watch.

findings.title: Google spend was concentrated on a single keyword
findings.description: Over the prior 30 days, $519 of $574 in Google spend went to one broad-match keyword (bartenders for hire). The other ~25 keywords in the campaign got either zero or negligible volume. The algorithm couldn't spread bets because it didn't have enough conversion signal to learn from. This is what drove the bid strategy change at end of period.

actions.title: Switched Google to manual CPC
actions.description: Moved off Maximize Conversions to manual bidding to break the single-keyword concentration and give every keyword a fair shot.

actions.title: Set per-keyword max CPCs based on top-of-page estimates
actions.description: Bid each keyword at roughly its top-of-page CPC so we compete for visible placements rather than buried ones.

actions.title: Paused 5 keywords with unreachable top-of-page CPCs
actions.description: Removed keywords whose top-of-page CPC was meaningfully above what the $40/day budget can sustain. Worth revisiting if budget grows.

actions.title: Added UTM tagging to Google ads at the account level
actions.description: Google traffic will now appear in PostHog with proper source attribution starting next report.

actions.title: Identified a PostHog tracking gap and queued the fix
actions.description: Found that bookings weren't stitching into the PostHog funnel view correctly. Fix is queued for the next development sprint.

nextSteps: Let manual CPC settle for 7 to 10 days before reading the numbers — daily fluctuations will be noisy at first.
Verify Google traffic is appearing in PostHog with proper UTM attribution.
Discuss a Meta creative refresh — details in the recommendation below.
Pull the Google search terms report to see what queries the manual bids are catching.

recommendation.title: Refresh the Meta creative
recommendation.context: Meta is the reach play on this campaign, but the current videos cap how many of those impressions can convert. 17% of viewers make it past the first 3 seconds. CPMs are $27 (high for this category) primarily because Meta's auction penalizes lower-quality creative. Fixing the creative compounds — lower CPMs AND higher CTR AND higher conversion rate from the same change.

changes.title: Produce 2 new short-form video concepts with stronger hooks
changes.description: First 3 seconds designed as standalone hooks (movement, on-screen text, sound design). Show the bar setup in action rather than opening with a static shot. Run alongside the existing creatives at equal budget for a clean comparison.
changes.impact: CTR lift from 0.86% to 1.5%+ would drop Meta CPA from $362 toward $150-200. Meta CPMs typically come down 20-30% on better-ranking creative, so the win compounds.

recommendation.timeline: Two concepts produced within one week of approval. 14 days of testing to declare a winner.
whatWeNeed: Raw footage of bar setups in action — not just static brand shots.
